title: bug: a seat whose own daemon died adopts whatever daemon now holds that port — px4swarm worker-9a70fc93 registered with the moes daemon, coded moes task V11, and left its bytes unlanded
description:
Observed 2026-10-30. The human reports it has happened before.

What happened
- px4swarm's daemon (Windows PID 26004) is dead. D:/projexts/px4swarm/.moe/daemon.json still names port 9876 (bindHost 0.0.0.0, startedAt 2026-10-28T19:16Z). The moes daemon (PID 17468) now holds 0.0.0.0:9876.
- PyCharm launched `moe-agent.sh --role worker --project /mnt/d/projexts/px4swarm --worker-id worker-9a70fc93 --command claude --team px4swarm` (WSL agent mode). The seat registered with the MOES daemon (proj-3830fac7) and created a team named "px4swarm" there. It then claimed moes task task-e493ed19 (CQ-V11) and completed it at 07:33:25Z.
- V11's two new files are untracked in the moes checkout (packages/moe-daemon/src/__acceptance__/mcpCall.ts and producerConsumer.acceptance.test.ts), and task.commits is empty, because the wrapper lands in its own --project (px4swarm, whose tree is clean). Attempt attempt-70f49183 sat in `finalizing`, so QA skipped V11, and the wrapper's next claims were refused with ATTEMPT_FINALIZING every 30 s.
- The seat's Serena ran on /mnt/d/projexts/px4swarm, with a 4 m 35 s startup, and wrote the moes handoff memory task-task-e493ed19…-handoff into px4swarm's .serena/memories.

Root cause: no client checks that the daemon it reaches serves its project.
1. scripts/moe-agent.sh `probe_daemon_health` (~line 1447, used at ~1524 for a Windows-owned daemon.json) passes on `status == 'healthy'` and ignores the reply's `projectPath`. Here the reply said "D:/projexts/moes".
2. moe-proxy `readDaemonInfoResult` (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:116) compares the projectPath written in the file with its own project. That always matches for a stale file. It never asks the daemon it connects to.
3. The daemon's /mcp accepts any client and carries no project identity. Optional hardening: a project parameter on the upgrade, refused on mismatch. That is the architect's call.
Check the IDE plugins' daemon adoption for the same gap: the px4swarm PyCharm window may have attached to the moes board the same way.

Required behavior: a client that reaches a daemon serving a different project treats its daemon.json as stale. It never registers, claims or bridges. It states which project that daemon serves and what to do: restart this project's daemon, which takes the next free port. Compare paths with the existing comparable-path rule (D:\x == D:/x == /mnt/d/x; see comparableProjectPath).

Containment done by the governor: V11's two files are declared onto V11 (moe.declare_files), so the next session holding V11 lands them.
definitionOfDone: moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 never adopt a daemon whose live identity (/health projectPath) is another project. Pre-flight stops before registering, with a message naming both projects. The launcher tests cover a healthy-but-foreign daemon, and scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes.

moe-proxy refuses to bridge to a daemon serving another project. It checks the live daemon's identity, not only daemon.json, and exits with the same class of error as today's daemon.json project mismatch. A unit test covers the foreign-daemon case.
The JetBrains plugin's daemon adoption is checked for the same gap, and either fixed with a ./gradlew test case or shown in the task comments not to need it.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT scripts/moe-agent.sh. Change only the daemon pre-flight.

1. probe_daemon_health takes an optional third argument, the expected project.
- Exit 0: healthy, and the served path is either the same project or cannot be judged. Callers that pass no project get exactly today's verdict.
- Exit 1: unreachable, timeout, unhealthy without a judgeable path, non-JSON, or a body over 64 KiB.
- Exit 3: foreign. Print the served projectPath on stdout.
- Foreign applies to any parseable reply, a 503 included. urllib raises HTTPError for a 503, so read the body with e.read().
- In the python, read at most 65537 bytes, with a 3 s timeout.

2. The comparable-path rule mirrors comparableProjectPath in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts and in the daemon. Use ntpath and posixpath explicitly, never os.path, so Windows python under Git Bash behaves the same.
- A drive path: ntpath.normpath, then '\' becomes '/', the trailing '/' is stripped, and the result is lowercased.
- A UNC path: normalize it with ntpath.
- Any other absolute path: posixpath.normpath, then /mnt/<d>/rest maps to <d>:/rest, lowercased.
- A served path that is not absolute cannot be judged.
- On msys/cygwin PROJECT is /d/..., so pass the expected project as `cygpath -m "$PROJECT"`. Never refuse because of a spelling difference.

3. Foreign (Windows-owned daemon.json) loop.
- rc 3: refuse at once. Print the MOE_DAEMON_FOREIGN_PROJECT block and exit 1.
- rc 0: adopt as today.
- Anything else: try the next candidate.
- Capture rc without tripping set -e: `rc=0; SERVED=$(probe_daemon_health ...) || rc=$?`.

4. PID branch. After kill -0 succeeds, and only when DAEMON_PORT is numeric, probe ${MOE_DAEMON_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:$DAEMON_PORT with the project.
- rc 3: refuse the same way.
- Anything else: RUNNING=true, as today.

5. The refusal block. Its three sentences are byte-identical in moe-agent.ps1:
- `[ERROR] MOE_DAEMON_FOREIGN_PROJECT: the daemon at <host>:<port> serves <served>, not this project (<PROJECT>).`
- `<DAEMON_INFO> is stale: this project's daemon is not running. Start it (the IDE's Restart Daemon, or moe-daemon start --project <PROJECT>); it takes the next free port.`
- `Refusing to register, claim or bridge to another project's daemon.`
The block deletes nothing, starts nothing and exports nothing.

Error handling:
- Every probe failure is unknown and keeps today's behavior. Only a positive, judgeable mismatch refuses.
- --no-start-daemon still skips the whole block. The proxy's own probe (task-86093c3e) covers that path and every later RPC.

Other peers edit other regions of this file, so preserve their bytes. Leave the fix-options wording to task-724e31fa.

3. Error handling: any probe failure means unknown. A refusal deletes nothing and starts nothing.

4. Keep the file UTF-8 with a BOM (scripts/CLAUDE.md), and keep the refusal text ASCII.

Planning split (architect-bd1eb82d, 2026-10-30). The fix spans three clients and three packages, about 9 files, so I sliced it on the package seam. This row keeps the wrapper slice and verifies the whole bug last.

- JetBrains slice, DoD 3: task-90664db1. I checked the plugin and the gap is real. MoeProjectService.connect/connectWithRetry adopt daemon.json's port whenever isProcessAlive(pid) && isPortOpen(port), with no identity check, so a reused PID attaches the window to another board. Under the PROTECTED profile, activationRefusal already refuses an unrecorded daemon; LEGACY does not.
- VS Code has the same gap with no PID check at all. It is filed as BACKLOG task-80ed1fe8 for the human to schedule.

This row dependsOn task-86093c3e and task-90664db1. task-724e31fa now dependsOn this row, because both edit the foreign-daemon probe block of moe-agent.sh. CQ-RF04 (task-de91373a) now dependsOn task-90664db1, because both edit MoeProjectService.kt.

Rule shared by all slices: /health reports the daemon's raw --project, which can be relative. A relative served projectPath is 'unknown', never 'foreign'. Only an absolute path (drive, UNC or POSIX) that differs by the comparable-path rule refuses.
